title: Business Wheel puts employee-built AI agents to work as the UAE moves to agentic AI
summary: 37 agents built by staff in six departments have delivered an estimated 152 hours of verified work for about $100 in AI costs, and are designed to carry more than a full-time role’s workload

contentHtml:
Since going live, most of them in September, the agents have produced more than 2,300 tasks. Image Courtesy: Business Wheel

37 agents built by staff in six departments have delivered an estimated 152 hours of verified work for about $100 in AI costs, and are designed to carry more than a full-time role’s workload

Press Release

DUBAI, UAE – As the UAE Government moves half of its sectors, services and operations to agentic AI within two years, and Dubai rolls out its private-sector Agentic AI transformation programme, Dubai-headquartered Business Wheel today shared the first results of its own: AI agents built by its employees, for their own jobs. Following a company-wide AI Bootcamp on September 28, 2026, staff in six departments built 37 agents that monitor markets, draft Arabic and English content, write software test cases, plan daily work and handle routine requests. Since going live, most of them in September, the agents have produced more than 2,300 tasks, comments and messages, which the company estimates replaced about 152 hours of real work.

Instead of a central rollout, Business Wheel asked the people who do each job to build the agent that helps them do it. A quality-control engineer built Testology, which drafts test cases from user stories and cut preparation time per story from about 60 minutes to 20 or less. A Daily Task Orchestrator built in the technology team reduced daily planning from about an hour to 15 minutes. In marketing, the TaQa Content Manager cut the time spent on each content item from 20 minutes to between five and eight, while a senior video editor’s Tools Geek agent saves about 40 minutes on every weekly AI-tools research run. Other agents handle leave requests, scan the creative team’s knowledge base each week, and track SEO and backlink opportunities.

The busiest agents run on schedules. One monitored Libyan energy and economy sources around the clock for more than five weeks, checking as often as every hour, and logged hundreds of bilingual incident reports for an energy news platform the company manages. A writing pipeline turned verified incidents into at least 17 Arabic and English article drafts, six of which have been published after human review. Another agent identified 112 backlink and directory opportunities for Business Wheel’s own website.

Business Wheel measured the results conservatively. The company counted every task, comment and message the agents produced, valued them with the time-saved benchmark of ClickUp, the work platform the agents run on, and then removed routine “nothing new” checks, repeated verifications and setup conversations, which made up more than half of the raw total. The remaining 152 hours are worth about $7,600 at ClickUp’s benchmark rate of $50 an hour, against roughly $100 in estimated AI running costs.

Business Wheel says the approach is built for the pace the UAE has set. Agentic AI describes software that plans and carries out tasks rather than only answering questions, and that is how the company’s agents work: they run on schedules, log their work in shared task lists and hand finished drafts to a person for approval. Its lessons for other UAE businesses are simple: let the people who own a process build its agent, count only work that delivered something, and give every agent a defined shift with its hours reported every month.

“The UAE has been clear that agentic AI is how government and business will work next, and we did not want to wait for it to be handed to us,” said Yasser Nasr Aldin, CEO of Business Wheel. “Our people built agents for the work they know best, and we refused to count activity as achievement: we measured only what the agents actually delivered. That is the same discipline we bring to our clients’ transformation programmes across the UAE and the region.”

“The bootcamp turned AI from a demo into a teammate,” said Ahmed Samy Hamada of Business Wheel’s marketing team, who built the company’s SEO and energy-news agents. “Some of our agents already work around the clock. Our next job is to give every agent a clear shift and measure it every month.”

Business Wheel plans to give every agent a defined role and schedule, retire agents that are not in use, and report agent hours monthly. At the pace its agents have already shown, the company estimates they will free up about 700 hours of work a year, rising to about 1,250 hours once every agent has a defined job. On paper, the jobs the agents were built for already add up to more than a full-time role’s workload, about 200 hours a month, and the company is using about a third of that today. Business Wheel is also bringing the same build-it-yourself approach to the digital transformation and automation work it delivers for clients.

About Business Wheel

Business Wheel is a business development and transformation firm headquartered at Meydan Grandstand in Dubai, with teams in Egypt and Turkey. For more than a decade it has helped growth-stage, legacy and distressed companies grow through business strategy and development, digital transformation and automation, fundraising and fund management, turnaround solutions, brand and commercial production, and HR solutions and competency frameworks. The Business Wheel group includes Anchor, Med Wheel, Fund Wheel and The Harvest. Learn more at bsnswheel.com.

UAE context

UAE Cabinet, 23 April 2026: a new federal framework to move 50% of UAE Government sectors, services and operations to agentic AI within two years (uaecabinet.ae).

Dubai Media Office, 12 October 2026: Dubai’s private-sector Agentic AI transformation programme, overseen by Dubai Chambers, includes training tracks for more than 14,000 member companies; 11 Dubai companies have pledged to integrate agentic AI into their operations (mediaoffice.ae).

How the hours were measured

Every record each agent authored in the workspace was counted. ClickUp’s own September 17 benchmark for five agents (77 hours 47 minutes) was divided by those agents’ posts up to that date, giving about 9 minutes of human work per post, and that rate was applied to all usage. Posts that delivered nothing new (routine checks, repeated verifications, setup and troubleshooting conversations) were then removed; shares for the three highest-volume agents come from a review of about 200 posts, and the rest were classified exactly. Four agents use the before-and-after times their owners logged. Private conversations between employees and their own agents are not visible, so the figures are a floor. Values represent capacity freed, not cash saved.
